source_evidence.observation: The input format has precision t, unit roundoff u = 2^(-t), normalized range endpoints f_min and f_max, and underflow envelope g_min = f_min/2 without subnormals or u f_min with gradual underflow. Assuming no overflow, input conversion satisfies fl(x) = x(1+delta)+eta with |delta| <= u, |eta| <= g_min, and eta delta = 0.

source_evidence.anchor: equation (2.4) and the following rounding-mode paragraph
source_evidence.observation: The accumulation format has T >= t, exponent range containing the input exponent range, U = 2^(-T), and G_min = F_min/2 without subnormals or U F_min with gradual underflow. Accumulation operations use the analogous U,G_min model. The displayed models assume round-to-nearest; directed rounding is covered only after replacing the corresponding bounds by twice their values.

The analyzed algorithm scales A and B by nonsingular diagonal matrices Lambda and M, rounds the scaled operands to the input format, performs their matrix product, and unscales. Scaling factors are powers of two. The surrounding text assumes A, B, and C are stored exactly in sufficiently high precision before and after the scaling operations.

The recommended largest overflow-safe scale is theta = min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)). For a length-n inner product, scaled input conversions satisfy componentwise bounds |Delta x| <= u lambda |x| + g_min and |Delta y| <= u mu |y| + g_min. After unscaling, the input-underflow quantity is omega = theta^(-1) g_min.

Each accumulation underflow contributes at most 4 theta^(-2) G_min ||x||_infinity ||y||_infinity after unscaling, and the number r of such underflows in one inner product satisfies r <= n. The full normwise estimate (3.24) contains the input-underflow and accumulation-underflow envelopes later used in Theorem 3.1.

Theorem 3.1 gives an exact displayed normwise bound (3.25). Equation (3.26) is explicitly obtained by dropping second-order terms and retains 2u + nU, 4n^2 theta^(-1) g_min, and 4n^2 theta^(-2) G_min.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph following equations (3.27)-(3.28), beginning 'Bound (3.26) thus recovers'
source_evidence.observation: The paper identifies 2u+nU as rounding error, 4n^2 theta^(-1) g_min as input underflow error, and 4n^2 theta^(-2) G_min as accumulation underflow error.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph beginning 'Several comments are in order'
source_evidence.observation: The paper conditionally states that when theta >= 1, theta^(-2) G_min <= theta^(-1) g_min, citing U <= u and F_min <= f_min, and concludes that the accumulation-underflow contribution is bounded by the input-underflow contribution. It separately presents theta >= 1 and the insignificance of accumulation underflows as expectations for most cases.

When underflow is included, the paper says only a normwise bound is available, and its overall claim that underflows should usually remain dominated by rounding errors is qualified as a practical expectation requiring suitable scaling.

ambiguities.issue: The less-than-or-approximately symbol in (3.26) has no locally quantified constant or remainder.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 7, printed B791, anchor: sentence preceding equation (3.26)] The paper says only that (3.26) results from dropping second-order terms, while (3.25) uses an exact <= inequality.
ambiguities.impact: A formal exact theorem should use (3.25), or explicitly define a truncation/asymptotic interpretation; silently reading (3.26) as an exact <= statement changes the source claim.

ambiguities.issue: U<=u and F_min<=f_min alone do not guarantee G_min<=g_min for every possible pairing of the piecewise underflow regimes.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 2, printed B786, anchor: equations (2.1)-(2.2)] g_min and G_min each independently use either a no-subnormal branch or a gradual-underflow branch. [PDF p. 7, printed B791, anchor: comparison paragraph] The paper nevertheless cites only U<=u and F_min<=f_min.
ambiguities.impact: The asserted comparison is directly justified when the branch choices are compatible, or whenever G_min<=g_min is separately known. If the input has gradual underflow but the accumulator lacks subnormals, an additional range condition is needed; a formalization must not infer G_min<=g_min from U<=u and F_min<=f_min alone.

ambiguities.issue: theta>=1 is an expected practical regime, not guaranteed by Theorem 3.1.

contract_plain_english: [PDF p. 7, printed B791, anchor: Theorem 3.1 and equation (3.26)] For the single-word, powers-of-two-scaled mixed-precision MMA computation, the paper's first-order normwise forward-error estimate consists of rounding error 2u+nU, input-underflow error 4n^2 theta^(-1)g_min, and accumulation-underflow error 4n^2 theta^(-2)G_min, all multiplied by ||A||_infinity||B||_infinity. [PDF p. 7, printed B791, anchor: paragraph beginning 'Several comments are in order'] In the conditional regime theta>=1, and provided the format definitions give G_min<=g_min, positivity permits multiplication by theta^2 and yields theta^(-2)G_min<=theta^(-1)g_min, so the accumulation-underflow envelope is no larger than the input-underflow envelope. [PDF p. 5, printed B789, anchor: discussion preceding equation (3.2); PDF p. 7, printed B791, anchor: comparison paragraph] The choice of the largest overflow-safe theta and the expectation that this condition usually holds are practical recommendations, whereas the envelope inequality itself is a conditional mathematical implication.
